title: Epiglottitis
stem: Paediatric resus. Nadia, 5, arrived with a 6-hour history of high fever and sore throat. She is sitting forward with her mouth open, drooling, and speaks in a muffled voice. Soft stridor. HR 150, RR 30, SpO2 94% in air, temperature 39.8 °C. She has not been vaccinated.
notes:
Checked against APLS, RCH Melbourne guidance on acute upper airway obstruction, and the Hib immunisation literature.

Epiglottitis (Hib in unvaccinated children; streptococci and staphylococci now): sudden high fever, toxic, drooling, muffled voice, tripod posture, soft stridor, little cough. The airway can obstruct completely at any moment. Do not lie the child down, examine the throat, cannulate, or do anything that upsets her; keep her with her parent, give oxygen without distress, and call the most senior anaesthetist and ENT surgeon for intubation in theatre (gas induction, with a surgical airway ready). Only after the airway is secured: cannula, blood cultures, IV ceftriaxone. Nebulised adrenaline may buy time. A lateral neck X-ray (thumb sign) is only for an uncertain, stable child and must never delay airway management. Notify public health for Hib; rifampicin prophylaxis for household contacts.

Your notes list epiglottitis as a Paedi gym topic and in the stridor differential (toxic, drooling, high fever) — this matches.

steps.label: Look only
steps.hint: Observe from a distance: posture, drooling, voice, stridor, colour.

Observe.r: Sitting forward on her father's lap, neck extended, mouth open, drooling.
Muffled 'hot potato' voice; no barking cough.
Observe.mark: Notes muffled voice without barking cough

Observe.t: Lie her flat and look at the throat with a torch
Observe.r: Lying flat and throat examination can cause complete obstruction.

steps.label: Call and prepare
steps.hint: Senior anaesthetist and ENT now, theatre, difficult airway kit including surgical airway; oxygen held by dad.

opts.t: Most senior anaesthetist and ENT surgeon to resus now; theatre alerted
opts.mark: Calls senior anaesthesia and ENT immediately

opts.t: Difficult airway kit, smaller tubes, needle/surgical airway kit ready
opts.mark: Prepares for a difficult and surgical airway

opts.t: Oxygen held near her face by her father, no mask forced
Keep her upright with her father; minimise interventions
opts.mark: Keeps the child calm and upright

opts.r: Distress may cause obstruction. Cannulate after the airway is secured.

opts.t: Lateral neck X-ray in the radiology department
opts.r: Never send a child with suspected epiglottitis away from airway expertise.

steps.label: After intubation in theatre
steps.hint: Cultures, ceftriaxone, PICU, public health, contacts.

opts.t: After gas induction and intubation: blood cultures, IV ceftriaxone 80 mg/kg, PICU
opts.mark: Antibiotics and cultures after the airway is secure

opts.t: Notify public health; rifampicin for household contacts (Hib); catch-up vaccination

qs.q: Classic lateral neck X-ray sign of epiglottitis?

qs.a: Gas induction in theatre, senior anaesthetist, ENT ready
wrong: RSI in the ED by whoever is most available
Awake fibreoptic nasal intubation in the ED
Symptoms that are worse at night and in cold air

badge.name: Hands Off
badge.flavor: Toxic, drooling, upright: don't touch, call the anaesthetist.

options: Lateral neck X-ray before anything else
Sitting forward, neck extended, leaning on hands

cards.q: Epiglottitis thumb sign is seen on…
options: AP soft-tissue neck X-ray with a grid
CT of the neck with contrast enhancement
cards.why: Only in a stable child with airway staff present.
